gap: No result ChatGPT got gives prices for the surge-per-pound leaders or works out dollars per surge watt. Today (2026-11-15) the OUPES Mega 1 (4,500 W surge, 27.8 lb) costs $699 at oupes.com, about $155 per kW of surge. The BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (3,600 W, 25.3 lb) costs $499, about $139 per kW. The Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (3,000 W, 24.9 lb) costs $529.99, about $177 per kW. OUPES also sells a Mega 1 Lite listed with the same 2,000 W / 4,500 W surge for $599.
standout_why: Volt & Valley's best-of-2026 page (cited) has prices for the C1000 Gen 2 ($529.99), DELTA 3 ($579) and Elite 30 V2 ($289.99). It gives no price for the OUPES Mega 1 ('Check price on Amazon'), does not list the Elite 100 V2 or the DJI Power 1000, and works out neither surge per pound nor dollars per surge watt. The two Tested Watts comparisons (both cited) list no prices at all and say surge duration is not stated. No rival page mentions the Mega 1 Lite, or that DJI's spec page caps sustained overload at 2,600 W for 30 to 60 s. Enough Watts could not be read because of a TLS certificate error.
decides: It confirms ChatGPT's surge-per-pound order (Mega 1 > DJI Power 1000 > Elite 100 V2 > DELTA 3 > C1000 Gen 2) and adds cost. The Mega 1 has the most surge per pound but costs $200 more than the Elite 100 V2 for 0.9 kW more surge and 2.5 lb more weight. The Elite 100 V2 has the cheapest surge per dollar among units with a sourced weight. The Elite 30 V2's '1,500 W' is BLUETTI's Power Lifting figure, not surge, so it should come out of a surge-per-pound ranking. DJI's 4,400 W is an instant peak. The highest output DJI says the Power 1000 holds is 2,600 W for 30 to 60 s, so it should not be treated as a 4.4 kW motor starter.
